children: U.S. stocks moved higher Tuesday, with technology shares providing enough momentum for the Nasdaq Composite to reach a fresh record high as investors continued to watch developments in the market and upcoming U.S.-China talks.

The Nasdaq was up about 0.6%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average each gained roughly 0.2%. Seven of the S&P 500's 11 sectors traded higher, led by consumer discretionary stocks, while energy was the weakest group.

Attention is also turning to a Sept. 24 meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. Trade policy, tariffs, Taiwan and artificial intelligence are expected to be among the issues discussed.
In the bond market, the two-year Treasury yield slipped one basis point to 4.74%, while the 10-year yield held near 4.95%. The 30-year yield rose one basis point to 5.28%.

The latest advance comes as higher Treasury yields remain a consideration for equity valuations. Investors are weighing whether elevated borrowing costs could limit further gains even as technology stocks continue to support the broader market.

title: Nasdaq Hits Record High Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
